edges.effect_quant: The better occupational syntheses show a repeated upward shift in ovarian-cancer risk with asbestos exposure, and the signal is stronger than a trivial observational blip.
edges.mechanism: Asbestos fibers can persist in tissue, drive chronic inflammation, and plausibly reach the female reproductive tract, creating a credible route to carcinogenic damage over long latency periods. This is one of the occupational-cancer links where biologic plausibility and pooled human data are aligned.
edges.summary: The most recent meta-analysis again found higher ovarian-cancer risk among women exposed to asbestos at work, echoing the earlier Environmental Health Perspectives synthesis. The literature is not enormous, but it is more consistent than many occupational-cancer signals and supports a harmful classification.
edges.caveats: Historical exposure measurement is imperfect, and some cohorts have limited adjustment for other occupational carcinogens. Even so, repeated pooled analyses have not erased the association, which argues against treating it as a chance finding.
